shopping: This is someone shopping with only a keyboard.
skip: They press Tab to move through the page… and the Add to cart button gets skipped.
scale: That's not rare. In 2026, 95.9 percent of the top million home pages had accessibility failures.
title: So we built Curb Cut.
It fixes barriers from the outside, right in your browser, and proves every fix works.
test: Step one. Kane, an AI testing agent, tries the keyboard. It fails.
control: Kane tries a mouse. The same task works.
So the website is broken for keyboard users.
rules: Step two. An agent writes safe rules: make the button reachable, and let Enter press it.
prove: Step three. Kane reaches the button, presses Enter, and the headphones go in the cart. A recording is proof.
share: Step four. The extension shares verified fixes with everyone.
mass-off: The hard barriers aren't single buttons. They're menus that only open for a mouse.
On mass.edu, a keyboard user reaches About, and the menu never opens.
The links are there, but invisible.
mass-on: With Curb Cut, the same keys open the menu, every link is visible as you reach it, and Enter takes you to the page.
mass-proof: Kane proved it both ways: without the fix it failed, with the fix it reached the page.
csc: On csc.gov.in, ABOUT blocked the keyboard too. Now it opens About MeitY.
reader: Screen reader users heard an unnamed box. Now it's called Sites search.
zoom: At high zoom, text ran offscreen. Now it wraps.
swatch: On ColorHexa, “I'm stuck” reports the picker. Kane verifies the fix.
results: Then we locked the code and pointed it at 2,050 websites it had never seen.
It found 142 real barriers and fixed 99 of them on its own, including 51 of the 89 hard ones: menus, expanding panels, tabs and pop-ups.
worms: On one of those new sites, the World Register of Marine Species, the keyboard skipped the Tools menu.
Kane failed it without the fix, and passed it with the fix.
verified: Fixes ship only after Kane proves them. 43 are live in the extension today.
retire: Every night, Kane tries each task with the fix turned off. When the website fixes itself, the patch retires. It becomes unnecessary.
close: Curb Cut. Fixing the web for the people it shuts out. Verified by Kane.
teaser-before: On mass.edu, press Tab to About. The menu stays shut.
teaser-after: With Curb Cut, the menu opens. Enter takes you to the page.
teaser-title: Curb Cut. Fixing the web for the people it shuts out.
